newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tankan shows Japan economy still improving -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Tankan shows Japan economy still improving -- BOJ.

text.p: The Bank of Japan's November "tankan" shows that overall, Japan's economy is gradually but steadily improving, Masayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's research and statistics department, said on Wednesday.
"Looking at the decisive factors for making judgments (on the economy), the economy is gradually recovering. It is gradual but steady," Matsushima told reporters.
Japanese companies are looking at more sales and profits, and corporate capital spending is also improving, not only for major manufacturers but for small and medium-sized firms as well, he said.
"Overall, the contents (of the data for business activity) are firm," he said.
But he said companies are cautious about their outlook, as seen in the forecast for major non-manufacturers' diffusion index for March of minus one.
Companies of all sizes have revised down their profit outlook for the latter half of this fiscal year, ending next March, he said.
"We are cautious about the outlook that overall, the firmness in the strength of the economic recovery is gradually increasing," Matsushima said.
He said that although the "tankan" itself cannot be the sole factor for determining the economic outlook, "the figures are not of the sort that show the economy will be losing momentum".
"However, the pace of recovery continues to be gradual, and we are not quite at the point where the economy is gaining more strength," he said.
He declined to comment on the BOJ's monetary policy.

Asked about the drop in long-term market interest rates following the release of the "tankan" this morning, Matsushima said the market was probably reacting to the view that the economy was unlikely to show substantial improvement in the coming months, as could be seen in the big manufacturers' diffusion index.
He added that as far as the long-term trend is concerned, there are positive factors emerging, such as improvements in corporate capital spending, supply and demand conditions, and company profits.

Asked whether the economy could move on to a self-sustainable recovery, Matsushima said: "The figures for the two engines for self-sustainable recovery, private consumption and capital spending, are rising."
Stock adjustments were proceeding steadily, and industrial production was recovering, he said.
He added that in the November tankan, the automobile sector and the ceramics industry, which supplies products for cars, contributed to the improvement in big manufacturers' business conditions.

"If such moves can be further secured, the cycle of production leading to increases in income and more consumption will override bad factors for the economy in the coming months. Though it (the economic recovery) may slow down, we will be able to maintain the recovery trend," he said.

Asked whether the BOJ has changed its economic assessment with the release of the tankan, Matsushima said: "There is no change in that the economy is gradually recovering, but data which confirms the firmness of the recovery is increasing."
Concerning corporate profit outlooks for the latter half of 1996/97, the impact of the weaker yen has contributed much to growth in exports, he said.
The currency rate at the time of the November survey was 106.66 yen to the dollar, which compared with 102.23 yen for the August tankan.
The reason for the lower profit outlook in the latter half of 1996/97 may be due to companies' expectations of a further strengthing in the yen.
